fieldValues.title: Whether poles need their own affirmation
fieldValues.decision_question: Should each pole of a domain's trade-offs be affirmed by the owner, or should a pole stand as a working default through the axis it refines, so the owner affirms only where a trade-off is placed on a domain's line?
fieldValues.context:
Affirmation is the owner's layer. A suggestion is forked into Affirmed, and nothing may affirm on the owner's behalf (c373c2c1, active; also 2800bea0, the handbook's "Human forks only" and RFC-046: createdBy is testimony, never authority). So an agent copying poles into Affirmed is already ruled out and is not an option here.

Poles are the hardest layer of a domain to affirm. Each carries its own claims, what leaning that way looks like (looks_like) and how it fails when overdone (shadow), and they only make sense against the whole domain. This is why the programme works with default axes. The owner ruled that "any domain inherits the base axes. We don't need to confirm these… working defaults" (06d83ca7), and that subdomains inherit their parents' axes and poles and localise the names (c020fd77).

In srs-programme on 2026-11-10, a human affirmed all 26 affirmed tensions. 17 of them contain 34 suggested poles, and none has an affirmed fork. They split three ways:
- 8 tensions (16 poles) refine an affirmed line that refines a base axis: Action, Change or Perspective. Their poles are local names of the base poles, but no pole-to-pole refines link says which is which.
- 3 tensions (6 poles) are compass axes of the Semantic records domain, whose definitions are ratified in the spec's decision compass.
- 6 tensions (12 poles) are in no domain and refine nothing. Only principles lean on them.

This is part of the open exercise "How do affirmations work?" (79140644), under "Which records start at the human tip, which rise to it, and which never need it?" (73be203b) and "How does setting up a domain become one affirmation instead of fourteen acts?" (179676eb). The owner calls it "a principle <> practical decision that we should make with care" (36bc6aae). On the cost: "They are often the most difficult layer of a domain to affirm. this is why we have been looking into working with default axes" (bdd19ab1).
fieldValues.friction:
- The repair in srs-programme#536 cannot finish: affirmed tensions read through suggested poles, and the tension card planned in srs-web#581 would show affirmed trade-offs whose sides are suggestions.
- Asking the owner to affirm every pole costs 34 of the hardest judgements, made in 17 sittings, for a structure the owner has already said comes by default.
- Doing nothing keeps the owner being asked about things they believe they settled ("I ratified them all yesterday?", 32683192).
fieldValues.alternatives_considered:
A. Do nothing: leave the 34 suggested poles inside the 17 affirmed tensions.
- Leads to: the layers stay mixed and each reader resolves it its own way. The owner keeps being re-asked. Pole: neither.

B. The owner affirms every pole: each of the 17 tensions is shown once in the srs-web#581 card with both poles, and one tick forks them.
- Leads to: Affirmed holds every pole. It costs 34 of the hardest judgements in 17 sittings. Six of the tensions sit in no domain, where the owner has said judging is not possible (be1cdc74). Pole: Semantic integrity, at the owner's cost.

C. Poles inherit: a pole is never affirmed on its own. It stands as a working default through the affirmed pole it refines. Agents add the missing pole-to-pole refines links as suggestions that the owner sees in the card. A pole with no such lineage does not stand: it waits until its tension is placed on a domain's line, and that placement is the owner's one act.
- Leads to: no owner acts now. The 16 inherited poles stand through their lineage. The 6 compass poles and the 12 poles in no domain wait until their tension is placed on a domain's line; placing a compass axis is a light check, because its definition is ratified in the spec. Affirmed keeps meaning "the owner judged this", and the owner's acts go to domains and their lines. Pole: Semantic integrity; meaning stays at the axis and the default is read from it.

Excluded by ruling: an agent forking the poles into Affirmed, with or without a provisional hold. Nothing may affirm on the owner's behalf (c373c2c1).
fieldValues.key_requirements:
- Affirmed must mean that the owner judged this.
- The owner's load must fall (SP-102; finding deedb2d5: up to 14 acts per domain), most of all on the hardest layer.
- Follow the default-axes rulings (06d83ca7, c020fd77): inherit, then localise the names.
- A judgement needs its domain (be1cdc74, a2225a2a).
- One way per goal: no second meaning of affirmed.
- The risk in C: an agent's refines link decides which local pole maps to which base pole. That orientation is a claim, so it stays a suggestion and is shown in the card, where the owner can correct it.
- Placed on Versioning and Reference, lean b3ac3391 "Semantic integrity over practical expression" ("Meaning should always reside at the meaning layer"): C keeps the meaning at the axis, where it already stands.
fieldValues.decision_statement: A pole is never affirmed on its own: it stands as a working default through the affirmed pole it refines, or waits until its tension is placed on a domain's line by the owner.
fieldValues.rationale: The owner already ruled that axes and their poles come by default and are refined locally. Asking for each pole repeats the hardest judgement many times over, and for six of these tensions it asks for a judgement that has no domain to make it in. Under C, the owner affirms what only the owner can judge, a domain's lines, while poles take their standing from the axis they refine. That puts 34 hard acts down to none now, and at most 9 placements later (3 compass axes, whose definitions are already ratified, and 6 tensions in no domain), each made in its domain and only if that tension is ever placed.
fieldValues.next_steps: srs-programme#536 (step 2 becomes: add pole-to-pole refines links as suggestions; the compass and no-domain groups as above); srs-web#581 (the card shows each pole's inherited standing and its refines link); exercise 73be203b (which records never need the human tip).
